7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: F. Qd2.

The drawing resource is 130...Qd2!, keeping the queen on the second rank instead of drifting to e6. The point is that it covers the h2 escape square and stops White’s freeing idea of Kh4/e6. If White tries the game’s 131.Kh4, Black has 131...Qh2+ and White’s king is driven back; the queen can keep checking and also hit the f4-pawn. Meanwhile, if White immediately tries 131.e6, then 131...Qd8 ties the pawn down: 132.e7 Qxe7, and Black has eliminated the dangerous passer. The move 130...Qe6 allowed White’s 131.Kh4! Qh6+ 132.Nh5! setup, after which e6-e7 becomes decisive. Qd2 avoids that coordination and holds the draw.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: M. Qe2.

The drawing resource is to keep the queen active on the e-file and hit White’s e-pawn. After 130...Qe2, White cannot simply push 131.e6? because 131...Qxe6 wins the pawn. If White tries 131.Kh4, then 131...Qxe5 liquidates the dangerous passed pawn and leaves Black with enough checking and trading resources to hold, since the remaining rook+knight+pawn cannot force a win without the e-pawn. The losing 130...Qe6 allowed White’s king to walk to h4 and set up Nh5/e6, but Qe2 prevents that coordination.

In the position after 26 Qxc8 Rxc8 White has no Queen and Black’s a-pawn is
on a3.  After

129. e5 Qa2+ 130. Kh3

White’s King is on h3, the White rook is on f5 and the White f-pawn is
on f4, so the f-file is blocked for the rook.  The Queen is on a2 and its
a-file is blocked by the own pawn on a3.  The only checking squares which
are actually reachable from a2 are

* b3+  –  b3–h3,
* e6+  –  e6–h3,
* g2+  –  g2–h3,
* h2+  –  h2–h3,

g2+ and h2+ are immediately Kxg2 / Kxh2 and e6+ is the losing
130...Qe6+ that is played in the game.  The only safe way to keep the
perpetual is to keep the Queen on the 2nd rank – or on a1 – where it can
be shuttled to h2/ h1 and give a perpetual check.  In particular the
classic drawing shuffle is

130... Qa1!

and from a1 Black has  …Qh1+ etc., with the same perpetual obtained from
the whole family of 2nd-rank shuffles Qb2, Qc2, Qd2, Qe2, Qf2.  Of the
moves you list this is the move normally quoted, and it is the move
which is legal in the position.  The illegal a-file moves Qa3 Qa4 Qa5 Qa6
Qa7 Qa8 are blocked by the Black pawn on a3, and Qg2+ and Qh2+ lose the
Queen to the King.  Up to the notation used in the list this is A.  The
same drawing idea is obtained from the other legal 2nd-rank shuffles
Qb2, Qc2, Qd2, Qe2, Qf2 in the list, D-E-F-L-M.

6.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: G. Qa6. The drawing resource is to keep the queen flexible so it can swing to h6 with check after White’s king advances, while still neutralizing the e-pawn. For example, 130...Qa6! 131.Kh4 Qh6+ 132.Nh5 Qe6! stops e6 and leaves Black with enough counterplay; if 133.Nf6+ Kd8 134.Rf8+ Kc7, the king escapes. If White tries 131.e6 immediately, then Qxe6 removes the dangerous pawn and the queen can still give checks against the exposed king.

3.text:
After 129 e5 Qa2+ 130 Kh3 the black Queen on a2 is en prise to the
white Queen on c2

    Qc2–b2–a2

and it has to move at once.  The squares of the 2nd rank are all covered
by the White Queen on c2 and the squares

    b3 a4 c3 c4 d3 e4 f5 g6 h7

are also covered by the White Queen.  In particular the White Queen
covers the rook on f5.  The Queen can therefore not stay on the 2nd
rank and it cannot go to b3, c4, d5 ? e.g. e6 is a square which looks
safe but

    130 ... Qe6 131 Rf6!

wins the Queen because Qe6 attacks the rook on f5 and after Rf6 the
Queen is lost on f6.  After 131 Kh4 Qh6+ 132 Kg1 etc. White gets a
decisive initiative and in the real game the win is converted.

The only way to keep the ending drawn is to keep the Queen on the
a–file out of the White Queen's lines and out of the rook's attack.
That is the a–file retreat.  The classical drawing resource is the
one–step retreat

    130 ... Qa3

and essentially any a–file retreat does the same job, e.g. Qa1, Qa5,
Qa6, Qa7, Qa8, etc., which keeps the Queen on the a–file, keeps the
White Queen from winning it at once and allows Black to keep the
perpetual checking/defensive manoeuvre which was the basis of the
long repetition in the game.  Qa3 is the usual name for the resource.

Remark:  The same drawing idea is obtained with any a-file retreat
that is not covered by the White Queen, in the list Qa1 A, Qa7 B,
Qa6 G, Qa8 I, Qa5 J and Qa3 N, the first of which is normally quoted
as Qa3.  The moves Qg2, Qf2, Qd2, Qh2, Qe2 are illegal because the White
Queen on c2 blocks the 2nd rank and Qc2 is the queen sacrifice.

1.text:
The queen is already on the a2–e6 diagonal and after 129… Qa2+ the
white K is on g2.  After 130 Kh3 the immediate threats are

*  e5–e6  with promotion, and
*  Kh4 with the threat of a perpetual check on the h-file.

The e6 square is already controlled from a2,  a2–b3–c4–d5–e6, so that
control has to be kept after the queen moves.  In one move the squares
from a2 which still attack e6 are the diagonal a2–e6 itself and the
rank/file squares a6 and e2,

  a2–e6      and     a6–e6    and     e2–e6 .

e6 is the blunder that is given in the score.  The two moves which keep
the e6 control and at the same time keep the perpetual-checking
resources on the h-file are

* 130… Qa6   a6–h6 is a check after the inevitable … Kh4 and a6–e6 still
covers the promotion square, and
* 130… Qe2   e2–h2 is a perpetual check after … Kh4 and e2–e6 still
covers the promotion square.

In particular the classic drawing defence that is normally quoted is

130… Qa6!

and, up to transposition, 130… Qe2 ! is the same idea on the second
rank.  This is the defence that is missed by 130… Qe6.

In the diagram after

129 e5 Qa2+ 130 Kh3

White is K h3, Ng3, Rf5, e5  Black is Ke8 Qa2.  The e-pawn is the
only real winning try for White.  As soon as the queen quits the
e-file / 5th rank the pawn can go e6–e7 and the rook + knight will be
enough for a win.

The queen can stay on the a-file or on the e-file and keep the e-pawn
covered.  In particular the queen can be kept on the same rank as the
pawn

Qa5

so that the e5-pawn is at once under attack, Q a5xe5, and the pawn may
not be left on e5.  After … Qa5 White cannot play e6 with impunity,
e6 Qxe6 pins the Rf5 to the Kh3 in any case, and the usual
Rf8+–Kxf8–Qc5 etc.  continuations are met by perpetual checking on the
a-file.  The same idea is obtained with the other covering squares

Qa6, Qa7, Qe2 and Qb2

which all keep e5/e6 under queen control and therefore keep the
rook+knight+ pawn vs queen ending drawn.  Qa5 is the textbook
waiting / covering move and is the one normally quoted.  Qa6, Qa7,
Qb2 and Qe2 are the same type of drawing cover; Qa8 is illegal by self
check and Qg2/Qh2 are losing checks.

The move most often quoted is the immediate cover

J. Qa5

which, up to the essentially equivalent Qa6/Qa7/Qe2/Qb2, is the
drawing resource.  The blunder Qe6 pins the Rf5 to the Kh3 and allows
Kh4 and the winning continuation that was played in the game.

* a6 – a6-e6 on the 6th rank,  and
* e2 – e2-e6 on the e-file.

Both squares keep the pawn covered and keep a checking shuttle to the h-file: e2 can go to h2 after Kh4, a6 can go to h6 after Kh4.  Qe6 itself is the blunder quoted in the game because 131 Rf6 etc. wins the queen.

Qa1, Qb2 etc. are the perpetual shuffles mentioned by several colleagues but they do not keep e6 covered and are losing to the pawn push.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The position after 129 e5 Qa2+ 130 Kh3 is White Kh3 Rf5 Ng3 e5 f4 vs Black Ke8 Qa2 a3 with White to have just escaped the check on g2. The queen on a2 is in front of the own a-pawn, so the a-file is closed upwards. From a2 the queen can go to a1, b1, b2-c2-d2-e2-f2-g2-h2 and on the a2-b3-c4-d5-e6 diagonal. Moves Qa3-Qa4-Qa5-Qa6-Qa7-Qa8 are therefore illegal because the a-pawn on a3 blocks the file, and Qg2+ / Qh2+ are immediate losing checks to Kxg2 / Kxh2.
